items.mnemonic: ONE line is drawn across the city gate, a STOP sign is planted beside it, and a clerk waits to STRIKE his gavel on anyone who ignores the rule. Lines, signs and gavels: that is POLITICS at work.
Everyone wants to SAY something: a SHEEP bleats its point from the back row, and your EGO shouts back from the front. The hall buzzes until the chair calls for orderly DELIBERATION.
A single primitive: the POPULACE itself, a crowd of figures packed shoulder to shoulder in the town square, waiting to be counted. The PEOPLE.
Down the ROAD rolls one CAR, then another hitched behind it, then another, bumper to bumper, until the whole line of cars seems to CONNECT into one long train.
A page of WRITING on the left and an INCH ruler on the right, facing each other across the desk like two debaters who refuse to blink. Each sits OPPOSITE its partner.
You STAND at the counter, state your business with your MOUTH, and the clerk points you across TOWN to a different building. Every office handles one SECTION.
A PERSON lowers a lid, ONE flat line, onto a MOUTH-shaped jar. It settles with a soft click, not a hair of space around the rim: a perfect FIT.
Under a LID-shaped awning, bolts of CLOTH hang from every stall while traders call out their prices over the crowd. Awnings and cloth as far as you can see: you are in the CITY.
A door FRAME stands open in the rain, and a PERSON ducks through it and shakes off the water. Now they are INSIDE.
A TREE on the left and an EYE on the right watch each other across the yard, each measuring how much the other has grown since spring. A MUTUAL gaze.
Under the ROOF someone draws ONE chalk line on the floor and plants a STOP sign right on it: nothing in this house moves past that mark again. The matter is FIXED.
An ENCLOSURE wall with a smaller MOUTH-shaped box spinning inside it, like a whirlpool seen from above, ring within ring. Everything in here makes a TURN.
By the ROAD a SNAKE and a second SNAKE lie coiled on a tray held up by TWENTY fingers, while EIGHT judges circle them, pointing at their favorite. Only one can be the winner: they must CHOOSE.
Under the ROOF a farmer stacks THREE shelves with the real harvest, and a PERSON stands guard so nobody swaps in painted wax. What is stored here is the TRUTH.
At the GATE a bull lowers its HORNS and the guard raises his staff toward HEAVEN: nobody passes without showing papers. This checkpoint on the old highway is the BARRIER.
WATER floods the yard; you grab a BROOM and sweep with BIG strokes toward the drain. Left gutter or right gutter? The water will go wherever you DECIDE.
A PERSON spreads a tent roof over the KING so that not one drop of rain touches him, from crown to boots. Nothing left out, nothing damaged: he is kept WHOLE.
A fresh green SPROUT is embroidered on the front of a coat of CLOTHES, worn so that everyone on the street sees it first. The decorated outer side is the SURFACE.
Banners topped with HORNS flutter over a RICE FIELD where TEN flags have been planted in rows, and a lone HALBERD stands upright in the mud. The harvest is forgotten: this ground is set for WAR.
A THREAD stretched taut, a RIGHT HAND guiding it down to a peg hammered into the EARTH: the warp line a weaver sets before the shuttle can PASS THROUGH.
The SUN climbs to its peak; below it an EAR tilts and a RIGHT HAND cups behind it to catch the faintest noon bell. The highest point of the whole day: the MOST.
The KING steps out onto the balcony so the crowd can SEE him in the flesh, not in a portrait or a rumor. He is PRESENT, here and now.
You SAY a note into a wooden FRAME packed with EARTH, and a MOUTH at the bottom hums it back a little flat. Adjust, listen, adjust again: that is how you TUNE.
A PERSON stirs a cauldron with a long SPOON; by the third stir the stew has turned gold and the stirrer has grown a fox tail. Something in this pot is bound to CHANGE.
A SMALL dart sits on top of a BROOM-shaped target of three bars, quivering dead center. It struck exactly where it was meant to: a HIT.
A THREAD tied around your finger, a WRAP of paper folded over it, and one DROP of red wax to seal the knot. Bound three ways, you will not forget this PROMISE.
WATER finds its level across the EARTH no matter whose PRIVATE field it crosses; rich plot or poor plot, it treats every one the same. That evenness is the LAW.
The HEART you are born with, beating from the first second of LIFE, decides how you meet the world long before anyone teaches you. That inborn core is your NATURE.
At the pass to the WEST a WOMAN stands with her hands on her hips, the only person who knows the way through the mountains. Nobody gets anywhere without her: she is what you NEED.
A COW is draped in CLOTH, and a SWORD trims the fabric to one set pattern: same length, same shape, every single time. Rules that cut everything to the same measure are a SYSTEM.
WATER is piped to every PRIVATE house, and the MOUTH of every well is kept swept and clean. A ruler who manages that much knows how to GOVERN.
A gatekeeper with a SPEAR, a drummer who must STRIKE the hour, a porter heaving with all his POWER: each has one job and nobody else will do it. That job is a DUTY.
A single primitive: BECOME. Watch a pile of raw timber turn into a standing gate with its last nail driven home, and you have seen a thing BECOME what it was meant to be.
A BASKET sits on the windowsill, and each night you paint one MOON on its side until the whole basket is covered in little moons. That span of nights is a PERIOD.
An EAR of ripe corn hangs on the stalk, and a RIGHT HAND reaches up, closes around it and plucks it clean off. TAKE.
An OLD man watches the SUN rise over a TOWN so large it spills past its own walls: temples, markets, and a palace at the heart of it all. This is the CAPITAL.
A sheaf of GRAIN stands beside a MOUTH: everyone at the table has rice to eat, so nobody quarrels over the last bowl. A full bowl keeps the HARMONY.
A TREE frame, a COCOON of silk thread hanging above it, a PERSON working the treadle, and a HALBERD-shaped lever that slams the beam home with every pass: a loom, the first MACHINE.
A single primitive: FLAT. A pole balanced across a stand with one weight on each side, so level that a marble set on it would not roll. Perfectly FLAT.
Put your POWER behind your MOUTH and shout encouragement from the sidelines; with every shout one more runner steps into the line. Each cheer is one more to ADD.
A CLAW from above lowers a parcel, a COVER of cloth lies between to soften the drop, and a RIGHT HAND below opens flat to catch it. RECEIVE.
A THREAD runs out of a SAMURAI's sleeve, slips under a COVER, and trails on between a pair of LEGS walking off down the road. The line never breaks: it must CONTINUE.
A SMALL BIRD hops along the ROAD, never once backward, one hop at a time toward the next town. ADVANCE.
Grains of RICE spill across the table, and a WOMAN taps each one with a chopstick, STRIKE after strike, counting under her breath. The total she reaches is a NUMBER.
Whatever you SAY slithers off like a SNAKE the moment it leaves your mouth. Pin it to paper before it escapes into the grass: a RECORD.
A bolt of new CLOTHES fabric lies on the table and a SWORD hovers, ready to make the opening cut. Nothing has been snipped yet: this is the FIRST.
A HAND lifts a SPOON toward the rising SUN to show a child exactly where to look. The part of the hand that does the showing is the FINGER.
A TREE staff with a cord BOUND UP around its top and a SMALL BIRD perched there as a crest: whoever carries this staff speaks with the voice of the court. AUTHORITY.
A RIGHT HAND holds up a TEN-shaped pole, a branch cut from the tree, wedging it under the sagging eave before the roof gives way. SUPPORT.
You STAND on the CLIFF edge and watch new LIFE push up through the rocky soil below until the whole hillside turns green. The land itself seems to PRODUCE.
A DIVINATION crack runs across a MOUTH-shaped turtle shell, and small FIRE flames beneath scorch it one spot at a time. Each scorch mark the fortune-teller reads is a POINT.
News of HAPPINESS is stamped with a red SEAL and pressed into a courier's RIGHT HAND to carry across town before nightfall. What he delivers is the REPORT.
WATER is poured over the WRITING of an old debt, a SWORD slices the soggy paper in TWO, and the halves float away downstream. The account is settled: FINISH.
Cold WATER splashed onto a dry TONGUE: the eyes fly open, color rushes back into the cheeks, and the whole body springs up LIVELY.
Below a CLIFF a WHITE spring bubbles up in SMALL ripples, then spreads out into a wide, grassy plain where the river begins. That open plain is the FIELD.
TWENTY hands lift a long temple bench and EIGHT more steady its legs; not one person could have moved it alone. TOGETHER.
STEP out at dawn as the SUN rises ONE finger above the horizon, measure it with an INCH ruler, and pocket the first coin of the day for your trouble. GAIN.
A rope has snagged on the HORN of a COW. Rather than hack it with the SWORD, you set the blade down and follow each loop until the knot slips free. UNTIE.
Under a LID-shaped straw hat, FATHER crosses his legs on the porch and swaps stories with the neighbors over the fence, trading gossip for vegetables. EXCHANGE.
On an ICE-cold morning the banker lets out a YAWN and counts out the SHELL money that will fund the next voyage. What he stacks on the counter is RESOURCES.
A bird's BEAK snaps up the worm before you can FINISH saying wait. It saw the moment coming and moved BEFOREHAND.
One short STROKE on top like a weathervane, a window FRAME beneath it, and a MOUTH inside calling out to whoever is coming up the path. The whole house seems to FACE TOWARD you.
On the HILL, under a full MOON, a RIGHT HAND lays an offering on the ALTAR at the very edge of the village: a ceremony held only on a special OCCASION.
By MOON-light, wearing a festival helmet with HORNS, the HUSBAND digs in his heels and hauls the tug-of-war rope with all his POWER until the other team slides over the line. WIN.
A single primitive: a festival MASK with a frame around the eyes and a bar down the nose. Tie it on and it becomes your FACE.
A COW opens its MOUTH and lets out a bellow that rolls across the whole valley, waking every farm. ANNOUNCE.
A RIGHT HAND presses flat against the CLIFF wall and pushes until the whole slab tips over backward. Pushing back against whatever stands in front of you: ANTI-.
A SWORD splits the tally stick in HALF; each party keeps one piece, and only a perfect fit of the two halves proves whose claim is true. JUDGE.
You SAY it out loud even though a BLADE seems to press against your HEART: yes, that mistake was mine. RECOGNIZE.
A PRIVATE visitor in a BIG straw hat, hair combed into three neat STREAKS, kneels among the other pilgrims at the shrine. PARTICIPATE.
A sharp SWORD sweeps through the ripe GRAIN and the harvest falls in neat rows at your feet. A quick cut and a full cart: PROFIT.
THREAD after thread is tied to the pegs of a SHELF until the loose strands are braided into one band that holds together. A GROUP.
A PERSON stands behind every word they SAY, with no contract and no witness needed. That is TRUST.
A seed of TALENT is pressed into the EARTH and left there. It does not wander off; it simply is, right where you planted it. EXIST.
A PERSON leads a COW before the magistrate: the cow ate the neighbor's cabbages, and someone has to rule on the MATTER.
A PERSON stands beside a SHELL-shaped treasure chest with a SWORD at the hip, guarding its flank through the night. SIDE.
A PERSON hands a heavy chest to a PORTER and walks on without looking back. From this moment the load is the porter's RESPONSIBILITY.
A BOW with a single straight STROKE beside it: the bowstring drawn back until the arrow tip touches the grip. PULL.
A single primitive: QUEST, a traveler in a fur coat with its tails flying as he sets out to ask for what is missing and will not come home without it. REQUEST.
A DOOR with an AXE leaning against it, marking the exact spot where the woodcutter lives. Ask anyone in the village and they point here: the PLACE.
Standing on the ICE in a long line, you let out a YAWN and shuffle one step forward as the window opens. Who is NEXT?
The SUN has set, and a SAW notches one more line into the doorpost: a day already gone and counted. YESTERDAY.
You SAY your case while unrolling a SCROLL of numbered points, one after another, so that nobody can lose the thread. ARGUMENT.
Under one ROOF sits a HEAP of stamped documents that only one person in the building is allowed to touch. That person is the OFFICIAL.
Pile more EARTH onto the bank, hang HORNS over the gate for luck, and the RICE FIELD baking under the SUN grows another row every year. INCREASE.
A PERSON holds a THREAD that runs in one slanting STROKE across to the next person, and on to the next, a single line linking the whole row. CONNECTION.
A HALBERD rings against ONE stone, every MOUTH in the hall falls silent, and the HEART jumps at the sound before the mind has caught up. FEELING.
A HEART colored deep BLUE, calm as the sea one hour and shifting with every tide the next. EMOTION.
